title.zh: 卷二百二十六 列傳第一百十四 海瑞 丘橓 呂坤 郭正域
title.en: Volume 226 Biographies 114: Hai Rui, Qiu Shun, Lu Kun, Guo Zhengyu
title.raw: 卷二百二十六 列傳第一百十四 海瑞 丘橓 呂坤 郭正域 Volume 226 Biographies 114: Hai Rui, Qiu Shun, Lu Kun, Guo Zhengyu

sentences.zh: 海瑞附:何以尚 丘橓 呂坤 郭正域

translations.literal: Hai Rui, with appended [biographies]: He Yishang, Qiu Shun, Lu Kun, Guo Zhengyu
translations.idiomatic: Hai Rui, with appended biographies of He Yishang, Qiu Shun, Lu Kun, and Guo Zhengyu

sentences.zh: 海瑞，字汝賢，瓊山人。

translations.literal: Hai Rui, whose style was Ruxian, was a man of Qiongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Hai Rui, styled Ruxian, was a native of Qiongshan.

sentences.zh: 舉鄉試。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He qualified in the provincial civil examination.

sentences.zh: 入都，即伏闕上《平黎策》，欲開道置縣，以靖鄉土。

translations.literal: Upon entering the capital, he immediately prostrated himself outside the palace gate and submitted the "Strategy for Pacifying the Li," wishing to open roads and establish counties to pacify his native land.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he reached the capital, he knelt outside the palace gate and presented his "Strategy for Pacifying the Li," calling for new roads and administrative counties to bring peace to his homeland.

sentences.zh: 識者壯之。

translations.literal: Those who knew of it admired his boldness.
translations.idiomatic: Men of insight praised his courage.

sentences.zh: 署南平教諭。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting instructor of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting district instructor at Nanping.

sentences.zh: 御史詣學宮，屬吏鹹伏謁，瑞獨長揖，曰：「台謁當以屬禮，此堂，師長教士地，不當屈。」

translations.literal: When a censor visited the academy, subordinate officials all prostrated themselves to pay their respects; Rui alone made a long bow and said, "An audience at the yamen should follow the protocol for subordinates, but this hall is the place where the teacher instructs his students—it is not fitting to bow low."
translations.idiomatic: When a touring censor came to the school, all the subordinate staff kowtowed in greeting. Rui alone made a formal bow and said, "At the yamen one pays respects as a subordinate, but this hall is where the master teaches his scholars—we should not abase ourselves here."

sentences.zh: 遷淳安知縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Chun'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed magistrate of Chun'an.

sentences.zh: 布袍脫粟，令老僕藝蔬自給。

translations.literal: He wore coarse cloth robes and ate simple grain, having his old servant grow vegetables for his livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: He dressed in plain hemp and ate simple grain, and had his elderly servant grow vegetables to support himself.

sentences.zh: 總督胡宗憲嘗語人曰：「昨聞海令為母壽，市肉二斤矣。」

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Hu Zongxian once told someone, "Yesterday I heard that Magistrate Hai bought two jin of meat for his mother's birthday."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Hu Zongxian once remarked to someone, "I heard yesterday that Magistrate Hai bought a whole two jin of pork for his mother's birthday feast.

sentences.zh: 宗憲子過淳安，怒驛吏，倒懸之。

translations.literal: Zongxian's son passed through Chun'an and, enraged at a post-station clerk, had him hung upside down.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongxian's son passed through Chun'an, he flew into a rage at a courier-station clerk and had him hung upside down.

sentences.zh: 瑞曰：「曩胡公按部，令所過毋供張。

translations.literal: Rui said, "Formerly when Lord Hu made his inspection tour, he ordered that nothing be supplied wherever he passed.
translations.idiomatic: Rui said, "When Lord Hu made his inspection rounds before, he ordered that no provisions be furnished along his route.

sentences.zh: 今其行裝盛，必非胡公子。」

translations.literal: Now his traveling party is lavishly equipped—he surely cannot be Lord Hu's son."
translations.idiomatic: This party's baggage is so lavish—they cannot be Lord Hu's son.

sentences.zh: 發雚金數千，納之庫，馳告宗憲，宗憲無以罪。

translations.literal: He confiscated several thousand taels of silver, deposited them in the treasury, and hurriedly reported to Zongxian, who had no grounds to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: He seized several thousand taels of silver, deposited them in the county treasury, and promptly reported the matter to Zongxian, who could find no cause to charge him.

sentences.zh: 都御史鄢懋卿行部過，供具甚薄，抗言邑小不足容車馬。

translations.literal: When Censor-in-Chief Yan Maoqing passed through on his inspection tour, the provisions offered were very meager, and Rui boldly declared that the county was too small to accommodate his carriage and retinue.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor-in-Chief Yan Maoqing toured the region, Hai Rui offered only the scantest hospitality and bluntly declared that the county was too small to accommodate his carriage and escort.

sentences.zh: 懋卿恚甚。

translations.literal: Maoqing was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Maoqing was furious.

sentences.zh: 然素聞瑞名，為斂威去，而屬巡鹽御史袁淳論瑞及慈谿知縣霍與瑕。

translations.literal: Yet having long heard of Rui's reputation, he restrained his wrath and departed, but instructed the touring salt censor Yuan Chun to impeach Rui and Huo Yuxia, magistrate of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had long heard of Rui's reputation and restrained his anger before moving on, though he instructed the touring salt censor Yuan Chun to bring charges against Rui and Huo Yuxia, magistrate of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 與瑕，尚書韜子，亦抗直不諂懋卿者也。

translations.literal: Yuxia was the son of Minister Huo Tao and, like Rui, was upright and refused to flatter Maoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxia was the son of Minister Huo Tao and, like Rui, was forthright and refused to flatter Maoqing.

sentences.zh: 時瑞已擢嘉興通判，坐謫興國州判官。

translations.literal: At the time Rui had already been promoted to vice-prefect of Jiaxing, but on these charges was demoted to assistant magistrate of Xingguo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Rui had already been promoted to vice-prefect of Jiaxing, but on these charges was demoted to assistant magistrate of Xingguo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，陸光祖為文選，擢瑞戶部主事。

translations.literal: After some time, when Lu Guangzu served as director of the Bureau of Appointments, he promoted Rui to secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later, when Lu Guangzu headed the Bureau of Appointments, he promoted Rui to a clerkship in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時世宗享國日久，不親朝，深居西苑，專意齋醮。

translations.literal: At that time the Shizong Emperor had reigned for many years without attending court in person, dwelling deep within the Western Park and devoting himself entirely to fasting and Daoist rites.
translations.idiomatic: By then Emperor Shizong had ruled for many years without holding court, secluding himself in the Western Park and devoting himself entirely to fasting and Daoist ritual.

sentences.zh: 督撫大吏爭上符瑞，禮官輒表賀。

translations.literal: Grand coordinators and governors vied to present auspicious omens, and the ritual officials invariably submitted congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governors competed to report auspicious omens, and the ritual officials unfailingly submitted congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 廷臣自楊最、楊爵得罪後，無敢言時政者。

translations.literal: Since Yang Zui and Yang Jue had been punished, no court official dared speak on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Zui and Yang Jue were punished, no one at court dared speak on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 四十五年二月，瑞獨上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the second month of the forty-fifth year, Rui alone submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the forty-fifth year of the reign, Rui alone submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞君者天下臣民萬物之主也，其任至重。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the ruler is master of all under Heaven—the officials, the people, and all things—and that his responsibility is exceedingly heavy.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the ruler is lord of all under Heaven, of officials and people and every living thing, and that his burden is exceedingly great.

sentences.zh: 欲稱其任，亦惟以責寄臣工，使盡言而已。

translations.literal: To fulfill this responsibility, he has only to charge his ministers with the duty of speaking their minds fully.
translations.idiomatic: To bear it worthily, he need only charge his ministers to speak their minds without reserve.

sentences.zh: 臣請披瀝肝膽，為陛下陳之。

translations.literal: Your servant begs to lay bare his heart and liver and set forth the matter for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to lay bare my heart and speak plainly to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝賢主也，賈誼猶痛哭流涕而言。

translations.literal: In former times Emperor Wen of Han was a worthy ruler, yet Jia Yi still spoke with tears streaming down his face.
translations.idiomatic: Even Emperor Wen of Han, a worthy ruler, was addressed by Jia Yi with tears streaming down his face.

sentences.zh: 非苛責也，以文帝性仁而近柔，雖有及民之美，將不免於怠廢，此誼所大慮也。

translations.literal: This was not harsh reproach, but because Emperor Wen's nature was benevolent and inclined toward gentleness; though he had the virtue of benefiting the people, he would inevitably lapse into negligence and decline—this was what Jia Yi greatly feared.
translations.idiomatic: This was no harsh rebuke: Wen's nature was benevolent and inclined to leniency, and though he had done good for the people, he risked slipping into negligence—this was what Jia Yi most feared.

sentences.zh: 陛下天資英斷，過漢文遠甚。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's natural endowment is keen and decisive, far surpassing Emperor Wen of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's natural gifts are keen and decisive, far surpassing those of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 然文帝能充其仁恕之性，節用愛人，使天下貫朽粟陳，幾致刑措。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Wen was able to fulfill his benevolent and forgiving nature, practicing economy and cherishing the people, so that strings of cash rotted and grain lay piled in storehouses throughout the realm, and punishments were nearly abolished altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wen was able to live out his benevolent and forgiving nature, practicing thrift and cherishing his people, until cash strings rotted in the treasuries and grain lay piled in the granaries, and corporal punishment all but ceased.

sentences.zh: 陛下則銳精未久，妄念牽之而去，反剛明之質而誤用之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, however, had been diligent in governing for only a short while before wayward thoughts drew you away, turning your naturally firm and clear character to mistaken use.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, however, had been diligent in governing for only a short while before delusion drew you away, turning your naturally firm and clear character to mistaken ends.

sentences.zh: 至謂遐舉可得，一意修真，竭民脂膏，濫興土木，二十餘年不視朝，法紀弛矣。

translations.literal: You came even to believe that transcendence could be attained, devoted yourself entirely to cultivating truth, drained the people's fat and marrow, wantonly launched construction projects, and for more than twenty years did not attend court—so that law and discipline have slackened.
translations.idiomatic: You came to believe transcendence was within reach, devoted yourself wholly to spiritual cultivation, drained the people's substance, launched construction projects without restraint, and for more than twenty years have not held court—so that law and discipline have collapsed.

sentences.zh: 數年推廣事例，名器濫矣。

translations.literal: In recent years the sale of offices by precedent has been extended, and titles and honors have been debased.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the sale of offices by precedent has spread, debasing titles and honors.

sentences.zh: 二王不相見，人以為薄于父子。

translations.literal: The two princes do not see each other; people regard this as neglect of the bond between father and son.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes do not meet; people take this as neglect of the bond between father and son.

sentences.zh: 以猜疑誹謗戮辱臣下，人以為薄於君臣。

translations.literal: You punish and humiliate your ministers on suspicion of slander; people regard this as neglect of the bond between ruler and subject.
translations.idiomatic: You punish and humiliate ministers on suspicion of slander; people take this as neglect of the bond between ruler and subject.

sentences.zh: 樂西苑而不返，人以為薄于夫婦。

translations.literal: You delight in the Western Park and do not return; people regard this as neglect of the bond between husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: You delight in the Western Park and do not return; people take this as neglect of the bond between husband and wife.

sentences.zh: 吏貪官橫，民不聊生，水旱無時，盜賊滋熾。

translations.literal: Officials are greedy and magistrates oppressive; the people can barely survive; floods and droughts come without cease; bandits grow ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Officials are corrupt and magistrates oppressive; the people can barely survive; floods and droughts strike without cease; banditry grows ever worse.

sentences.zh: 陛下試思今日天下，為何如乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, consider what the realm under Heaven is like today.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, consider what the realm is like today.

sentences.zh: 邇者嚴嵩罷相，世蕃極刑，一時差快人意。

translations.literal: Recently Yan Song was dismissed from the chancellorship and Yan Shifan executed—for a moment this somewhat pleased people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Yan Song was dismissed and Yan Shifan executed to the full extent of the law—for a moment this gave people some satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 然嵩罷之後，猶嵩未相之前而已，世非甚清明也，不及漢文帝遠甚。

translations.literal: Yet after Song's dismissal, the age is no better than before he became chancellor; the world is not very clear and bright, and falls far short of the age of Emperor Wen of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after Song's fall the age is no better than before he rose to power; the world is scarcely more enlightened, and falls far short of Emperor Wen's reign.

sentences.zh: 蓋天下之人不直陛下久矣。

translations.literal: For the people of all under Heaven have long ceased to regard Your Majesty as upright.
translations.idiomatic: For the people of the realm have long ceased to regard Your Majesty as upright.

sentences.zh: 古者人君有過，賴臣工匡弼。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when rulers erred, they relied on their ministers to correct and assist them.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when rulers erred, they relied on their ministers to set them right.

sentences.zh: 今乃修齋建醮，相率進香，仙桃天藥，同辭表賀。

translations.literal: Now you practice fasting and erect altars for Daoist rites; officials vie with one another to present incense; immortal peaches and celestial elixirs are greeted with congratulatory memorials in identical language.
translations.idiomatic: Now you practice fasting and erect altars for Daoist rites; officials vie to present incense; immortal peaches and celestial elixirs are greeted with identical congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 建宮築室，則將作竭力經營；

translations.literal: When palaces and halls are to be built, the Directorate of Public Works labors with all its strength at the task;
translations.idiomatic: When palaces and halls are to be built, the Directorate of Public Works labors at full stretch;

sentences.zh: 購香市寶，則度支差求四出。

translations.literal: when incense and precious objects are to be purchased, the Bureau of Revenue dispatches agents in every direction.
translations.idiomatic: when incense and precious objects are to be purchased, the Bureau of Revenue dispatches agents in every direction.

sentences.zh: 陛下誤舉之，而諸臣誤順之，無一人肯為陛下正言者，諛之甚也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has mistakenly undertaken these things, and the various ministers have mistakenly gone along with them; not one is willing to speak straight words to Your Majesty—this is flattery in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has mistakenly undertaken these things, and your ministers have mistakenly gone along; not one is willing to speak plainly to you—this is flattery in the extreme.

sentences.zh: 然愧心餒氣，退有後言，欺君之罪何如！

translations.literal: Yet with guilty hearts and deflated spirits, they speak differently in private—what of the crime of deceiving one's ruler!
translations.idiomatic: Yet with guilty hearts they speak differently in private—what of the crime of deceiving one's ruler!

sentences.zh: 夫天下者，陛下之家，人未有不顧其家者，內外臣工皆所以奠陛下之家而磐石之者也。

translations.literal: All under Heaven is Your Majesty's household; there is no one who does not care for his own household. The ministers within and without the court are all those who should lay the foundation of Your Majesty's household and make it firm as bedrock.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven is Your Majesty's household; is there anyone who does not care for his own home? The ministers within and without the court exist to secure your household and make it firm as bedrock.

sentences.zh: 一意修真，是陛下之心惑。

translations.literal: To devote yourself entirely to cultivating truth is a delusion of Your Majesty's mind.
translations.idiomatic: To devote yourself wholly to spiritual cultivation is a delusion of the mind.

sentences.zh: 過於苛斷，是陛下之情偏。

translations.literal: To be excessively harsh in judgment is a bias of Your Majesty's temperament.
translations.idiomatic: To be excessively harsh in judgment is a bias of temperament.

sentences.zh: 而謂陛下不顧其家，人情乎？

translations.literal: Yet to say that Your Majesty does not care for his household—is this in accord with human feeling?
translations.idiomatic: Yet to say that Your Majesty does not care for his household—is that in accord with human nature?

sentences.zh: 諸臣徇私廢公，得一官多以欺敗，多以不事事敗，實有不足當陛下意者。

translations.literal: The various ministers pursue private interest and neglect public duty; many who gain office end in ruin through deception, many through failure to perform their duties—there truly are those unworthy of Your Majesty's trust.
translations.idiomatic: Your ministers pursue private interest and neglect public duty; many who gain office fall through deceit, many through neglect of duty—there truly are those unworthy of your trust.

sentences.zh: 其不然者，君心臣心偶不相值也，而遂謂陛下厭薄臣工，是以拒諫。

translations.literal: In other cases, the ruler's mind and the minister's mind happen not to coincide, and they then conclude that Your Majesty despises and looks down upon his ministers, and on that account refuse to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: In other cases the ruler's mind and the minister's simply fail to meet, and they conclude that Your Majesty despises his ministers and therefore refuse to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 執一二之不當，疑千百之皆然，陷陛下于過舉，而恬不知怪，諸臣之罪大矣。

translations.literal: They seize upon one or two improprieties and suspect that a thousand or ten thousand are the same, trapping Your Majesty in wrongful actions while remaining placidly unaware that anything is amiss—the crime of the ministers is great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: They seize on one or two improprieties and suspect that all are alike, trapping Your Majesty in wrongful actions while remaining unaware that anything is amiss—the ministers' crime is great indeed.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰「上人疑則百姓惑，下難知則君長勞」，此之謂也。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites says, "When those above are doubtful, the common people are confused; when those below are hard to know, rulers and elders are wearied"—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says, "When those above are doubtful, the people are confused; when those below are hard to read, rulers are wearied"—this is what is meant.

sentences.zh: 且陛下之誤多矣，其大端在於齋醮。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty's errors are many; the greatest lies in fasting and Daoist rites.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty's errors are many; the greatest lies in fasting and Daoist ritual.

sentences.zh: 齋醮所以求長生也。

translations.literal: Fasting and Daoist rites are undertaken to seek long life.
translations.idiomatic: Fasting and Daoist ritual are undertaken to seek long life.

sentences.zh: 自古聖賢垂訓，修身立命曰「順受其正」矣，未聞有所謂長生之說。

translations.literal: Since antiquity the sages and worthies have handed down their teaching: in cultivating the self and establishing one's destiny they say one should "accept one's proper allotment in accordance with the Way"—never have I heard of any doctrine called long life.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity the sages have taught that in cultivating the self one should "accept one's proper allotment in accordance with the Way"—never have I heard of any doctrine of immortality.

sentences.zh: 堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武，聖之盛也，未能久世，下之亦未見方外士自漢、唐、宋至今存者。

translations.literal: Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu were the greatest of sages, yet they could not endure forever; below them, neither have I seen any Daoist adept from Han, Tang, or Song times who survives to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu were the greatest of sages, yet they could not endure forever; nor have I seen any Daoist adept from Han, Tang, or Song times who survives to the present.

sentences.zh: 陛下受術于陶仲文，以師稱之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty received the arts from Tao Zhongwen and addressed him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty received the arts from Tao Zhongwen and addressed him as teacher.

sentences.zh: 仲文則既死矣，彼不長生，而陛下何獨求之？

translations.literal: Yet Zhongwen is already dead; he did not attain long life—why should Your Majesty alone seek it?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhongwen is already dead; he did not attain long life—why should Your Majesty alone seek it?

sentences.zh: 至於仙桃天藥，怪妄尤甚。

translations.literal: As for immortal peaches and celestial elixirs, their absurdity and presumption are still greater.
translations.idiomatic: As for immortal peaches and celestial elixirs, their absurdity is still greater.

sentences.zh: 昔宋真宗得天書於乾祐山，孫奭曰：「天何言哉？

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Zhenzong of Song received a celestial book at Mount Qianyou; Sun Shi said, "What does Heaven speak?
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Zhenzong of Song received a celestial book at Mount Qianyou; Sun Shi said, "What does Heaven speak?

sentences.zh: 豈有書也！」

translations.literal: How could there be a book!"
translations.idiomatic: How could there be a book!

sentences.zh: 桃必采而後得，藥必制而後成。

translations.literal: Peaches must be picked before they can be obtained; medicines must be prepared before they can be made.
translations.idiomatic: Peaches must be picked before they can be had; medicines must be prepared before they can be made.

sentences.zh: 今無故獲此二物，是有足而行耶？

translations.literal: Now these two things have been obtained without cause—do they have feet and walk of themselves?
translations.idiomatic: Now these two things appear without cause—do they have feet and walk of themselves?

sentences.zh: 曰天賜者，有手執而付之耶？

translations.literal: If you say Heaven bestowed them, was there a hand that held them out and delivered them?
translations.idiomatic: If you say Heaven bestowed them, was there a hand that held them out and delivered them?

sentences.zh: 此左右奸人，造為妄誕以欺陛下，而陛下誤信之，以為實然，過矣。

translations.literal: These are wicked men at your side who fabricate absurd falsehoods to deceive Your Majesty, and Your Majesty has mistakenly believed them, taking them for real—this is going too far.
translations.idiomatic: These are wicked men at your side who fabricate absurd falsehoods to deceive you, and you have mistakenly believed them as real—this is going too far.

sentences.zh: 陛下將謂懸刑賞以督責臣下，則分理有人，天下無不可治，而修真為無害已乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty will say that by hanging rewards and punishments to supervise and hold your ministers accountable, duties are assigned to the proper persons and nothing under Heaven is beyond governance—so that cultivating truth does no harm?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty will say that by hanging rewards and punishments over your ministers, duties are assigned and nothing is beyond governance—so that spiritual cultivation does no harm?

sentences.zh: 太甲曰：「有言逆於汝心，必求諸道；

translations.literal: Tai Jia said, "When words run counter to your heart, you must seek their meaning in the Way;
translations.idiomatic: Tai Jia said, "When words run counter to your heart, you must seek their meaning in the Way;

sentences.zh: 有言遜於汝志，必求諸非道。」

translations.literal: when words accord with your wishes, you must seek their meaning outside the Way."
translations.idiomatic: when words accord with your wishes, you must seek their meaning outside the Way.

sentences.zh: 用人而必欲其唯言莫違，此陛下之計左也。

translations.literal: To employ men yet insist that they never speak except to agree—this is a mistaken plan on Your Majesty's part.
translations.idiomatic: To employ men yet insist that they never speak except to agree—this is a mistaken plan on Your Majesty's part.

sentences.zh: 既觀嚴嵩，有一不順陛下者乎？

translations.literal: Consider Yan Song: was there ever one word that did not accord with Your Majesty's wishes?
translations.idiomatic: Consider Yan Song: was there ever one word that did not accord with your wishes?

sentences.zh: 昔為同心，今為戮首矣。

translations.literal: Once he was of one mind with you; now he is executed and his head displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was of one mind with you; now he is executed and his head displayed.

sentences.zh: 梁材守道守官，陛下以為逆者也，歷任有聲，官戶部者至今首稱之。

translations.literal: Liang Cai upheld the Way and held to his office; Your Majesty regarded him as rebellious, yet in every post he served he won renown, and among those who served in the Ministry of Revenue he is still chiefly praised to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cai upheld the Way and held to his office; you regarded him as rebellious, yet in every post he won renown, and among those who served in the Ministry of Revenue he is still chiefly praised to this day.

sentences.zh: 然諸臣寧為嵩之順，不為材之逆，得非有以窺陛下之微，而潛為趨避乎？

translations.literal: Yet the ministers would rather be compliant like Song than upright like Cai—is this not because they have discerned something of Your Majesty's inner mind and secretly steer to avoid trouble?
translations.idiomatic: Yet your ministers would rather be compliant like Song than upright like Cai—is this not because they have discerned something of your inner mind and secretly steer to avoid trouble?

sentences.zh: 即陛下亦何利於是。

translations.literal: What benefit does Your Majesty gain from this?
translations.idiomatic: What benefit do you gain from this?

sentences.zh: 陛下誠知齋齋無益，一旦翻然悔悟，日禦正朝，與宰相、侍從、言官講求天下利害，洗數十年之積誤，置身於堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之間，使諸臣亦得自洗數十年阿君之恥，置其身於皋、夔、伊、傅之列，天下何憂不治，萬事何憂不理。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly knows that fasting is of no benefit and one day turns about in repentance, holding court daily and discussing with the chancellor, attendants, and remonstrating officials the benefits and harms to all under Heaven, washing away decades of accumulated error, placing yourself among Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, and enabling your ministers also to wash away decades of shame at flattering their ruler, placing themselves among Gao Yao, Kui, Yi Yin, and Fu Yue—what worry would there be that the realm would not be governed, what worry that affairs would not be ordered?
translations.idiomatic: If you truly know that fasting is of no benefit and one day turn about in repentance, holding court daily and discussing with your chancellor, attendants, and remonstrating officials the welfare of the realm, washing away decades of accumulated error, placing yourself among Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, and enabling your ministers to wash away decades of shame at flattering their ruler, placing themselves among Gao Yao, Kui, Yi Yin, and Fu Yue—what worry would there be that the realm would not be governed, that affairs would not be ordered?

sentences.zh: 此在陛下一振作間而已。

translations.literal: This depends on a single effort of renewal on Your Majesty's part.
translations.idiomatic: This depends on a single effort of renewal on your part.

sentences.zh: 釋此不為，而切切於輕舉度世，敝精勞神，以求之於系風捕影、茫然不可知之域，臣見勞苦終身，而終於無所成也。

translations.literal: You set this aside and do not do it, yet are earnest about lightly attempting to transcend the world, exhausting your spirit and wearing out your mind, seeking in the realm of tying down the wind and catching shadows, vague and unknowable—I foresee that you will toil your whole life and in the end achieve nothing.
translations.idiomatic: You set this aside and do not do it, yet are earnest about lightly attempting to transcend the world, exhausting your spirit and wearing out your mind, seeking in the realm of tying down the wind and catching shadows—I foresee that you will toil your whole life and in the end achieve nothing.

sentences.zh: 今大臣持祿而好諛，小臣畏罪而結舌，臣不勝憤恨。

translations.literal: Now the great ministers hold their salaries and love to flatter; the lesser officials fear punishment and hold their tongues—your servant cannot contain his indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Now the great ministers hold their salaries and love to flatter; the lesser officials fear punishment and hold their tongues—I cannot contain my indignation.

sentences.zh: 是以冒死，願盡區區，惟陛下垂聽焉。

translations.literal: Therefore, risking death, I wish to exhaust my humble effort—may Your Majesty deign to listen.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, risking death, I offer this humble effort—may Your Majesty deign to listen.

sentences.zh: 帝得疏，大怒，抵之地，顧左右曰：「趣執之，無使得遁！」

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the memorial, he was greatly enraged, dashed it to the ground, and turning to those beside him said, "Seize him at once—do not let him escape!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor received the memorial, he was furious, dashed it to the ground, and turning to those beside him said, "Seize him at once—do not let him escape!

sentences.zh: 宦官黃錦在側曰：「此人素有癡名。

translations.literal: The eunuch Huang Jin, standing beside him, said, "This man has long borne the reputation of a simpleton.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Huang Jin, standing beside him, said, "This man has long borne the reputation of a simpleton.

sentences.zh: 聞其上疏時，自知觸忤當死，市一棺，訣妻子，待罪於朝，僮僕亦奔散無留者，是不遁也。」

translations.literal: I hear that when he submitted his memorial, knowing he had given offense and must die, he bought a coffin, bade farewell to his wife and children, and waited at court to receive punishment; his servants too have scattered and none remain—he is not fleeing."
translations.idiomatic: I hear that when he submitted his memorial, knowing he had given offense and must die, he bought a coffin, bade farewell to his wife and children, and waited at court to receive punishment; his servants too have scattered and none remain—he is not fleeing.

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The Emperor fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 少頃復取讀之，日再三，為感動太息，留中者數月。

translations.literal: After a little while he picked it up and read it again, two or three times a day, moved to deep sighs; he kept it withheld at court for several months.
translations.idiomatic: After a little while he picked it up and read it again, two or three times a day, moved to deep sighs; he kept it withheld at court for several months.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「此人可方比干，第朕非紂耳。」

translations.literal: He once said, "This man may be compared to Bigan—but I am no King Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "This man may be compared to Bigan—but I am no King Zhou.

sentences.zh: 會帝有疾，煩懣不樂，召閣臣徐階議內禪，因曰：「海瑞言俱是。

translations.literal: When the Emperor fell ill, vexed and unhappy, he summoned Grand Secretary Xu Jie to discuss abdication in favor of the heir, and said, "Everything Hai Rui said is true.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor fell ill, vexed and unhappy, he summoned Grand Secretary Xu Jie to discuss abdication in favor of the heir, and said, "Everything Hai Rui said is true.

sentences.zh: 朕今病久，安能視事。」

translations.literal: I have been ill so long—how can I attend to affairs of state?"
translations.idiomatic: I have been ill so long—how can I attend to affairs of state?

sentences.zh: 又曰：「朕不自謹惜，致此疾困。

translations.literal: He also said, "I did not restrain and cherish myself, and brought on this illness and distress.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "I did not restrain and cherish myself, and brought on this illness and distress.

sentences.zh: 使朕能出禦便殿，豈受此人詬詈耶？」

translations.literal: Had I been able to go out and hold court in the side hall, how would I have endured this man's reviling?"
translations.idiomatic: Had I been able to go out and hold court in the side hall, how would I have endured this man's reviling?

sentences.zh: 遂逮瑞下詔獄，究主使者。

translations.literal: He then had Rui arrested and sent to the imperial prison, investigating who had instigated him.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Rui arrested and sent to the imperial prison, investigating who had instigated him.

sentences.zh: 尋移刑部，論死。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the case was transferred to the Ministry of Justice, which sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the case was transferred to the Ministry of Justice, which sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 獄上，仍留中。

translations.literal: When the sentence was submitted, it was again withheld at court.
translations.idiomatic: When the sentence was submitted, it was again withheld at court.

sentences.zh: 戶部司務何以尚者，揣帝無殺瑞意，疏請釋之。

translations.literal: He Yishang, a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, surmising that the Emperor had no intention of executing Rui, submitted a memorial requesting his release.
translations.idiomatic: He Yishang, a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, surmising that the Emperor had no intention of executing Rui, submitted a memorial requesting his release.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命錦衣衛杖之百，錮詔獄，晝夜搒訊。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged and ordered the Embroidered-Uniform Guard to beat him one hundred strokes, imprison him in the imperial prison, and interrogate him day and night under torture.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged and ordered the Embroidered-Uniform Guard to beat him one hundred strokes, imprison him in the imperial prison, and interrogate him day and night under torture.

sentences.zh: 越二月，帝崩，穆宗立，兩人並獲釋。

translations.literal: Two months later the Emperor died and the Muzong Emperor ascended the throne; both men were released together.
translations.idiomatic: Two months later the Emperor died and the Muzong Emperor ascended the throne; both men were released together.

sentences.zh: 帝初崩，外庭多未知。

translations.literal: When the Emperor first died, those outside the palace for the most part did not yet know.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor first died, those outside the palace for the most part did not yet know.

sentences.zh: 提牢主事聞狀，以瑞且見用，設酒饌款之。

translations.literal: The chief prison officer heard the news; learning that Rui was about to be put to use, he set out wine and food to entertain him.
translations.idiomatic: The chief prison officer, hearing what had happened and that Rui would soon be restored to office, prepared wine and a meal to welcome him warmly.

sentences.zh: 瑞自疑當赴西市，恣飲啖，不顧。

translations.literal: Rui himself suspected he was to be taken to the Western Market; he ate and drank freely without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Rui assumed he was bound for the Western Market execution ground, so he ate and drank his fill without a care.

sentences.zh: 主事因附耳語：「宮車適晏駕，先生今即出大用矣。」

translations.literal: The chief officer then whispered in his ear: "The imperial carriage has just borne the late Emperor; sir, you will immediately be released for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: The chief officer leaned close and whispered: "The Emperor has just died; sir, you are about to be released and given high office.

sentences.zh: 瑞曰：「信然乎？」

translations.literal: Rui said, "Is it truly so?"
translations.idiomatic: Rui asked, "Can that be true?"

sentences.zh: 即大慟，盡嘔出所飲食，隕絕於地，終夜哭不絕聲。

translations.literal: At once he was overcome with great grief, vomited up all he had eaten and drunk, collapsed to the ground, and wept all night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He broke into violent grief at once, vomited everything he had consumed, collapsed senseless to the floor, and wept without stopping through the night.

sentences.zh: 既釋，復故官。

translations.literal: Once released, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After his release, he was reinstated in his former post.

sentences.zh: 俄改兵部。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was moved to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 擢尚寶丞，調大理。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Office of Imperial Seals and transferred to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Office of Imperial Seals, then transferred to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，徐階為御史劉康所劾，瑞言：「階事先帝，無能救于神仙土木之誤，畏威保位，誠亦有之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing, Xu Jie was impeached by Censor Liu Kang. Rui said: "Jie served the late Emperor yet could not rescue him from the errors of pursuing immortality and palace construction; fearing authority and preserving his position—this is indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing, Censor Liu Kang impeached Xu Jie. Hai Rui said: "In serving the late Emperor, Xu Jie could not pull him back from his obsession with immortality elixirs and grand building projects, and he feared power enough to cling to office—that much is true.

sentences.zh: 然自執政以來，憂勤國事，休休有容，有足多者。

translations.literal: Yet since he took charge of government, he has been diligent in state affairs, gracious and tolerant—there is much to praise.
translations.idiomatic: But from the time he came to power he has toiled over state affairs with generous forbearance, and there is much in him to commend.

sentences.zh: 康乃甘心鷹犬，捕噬善類，其罪又浮于高拱。」

translations.literal: Kang, however, willingly serves as hawk and hound, seizing and devouring good men—his crime surpasses even Gao Gong's.
translations.idiomatic: Kang, by contrast, gladly plays the hawk and hound, hunting down and tearing apart the worthy—and his offense exceeds even Gao Gong's.

sentences.zh: 人韙其言。

translations.literal: People approved of his words.
translations.idiomatic: People widely agreed with what he said.

sentences.zh: 曆兩京左、右通政。

translations.literal: He served successively as Left and Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission in both capitals.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Left and Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission in both capitals in turn.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，以右僉都御史巡撫應天十府。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year, he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to oversee and pacify the ten prefectures of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year, he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator over the ten prefectures of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 屬吏憚其威，墨者多自免去。

translations.literal: Subordinate officials feared his authority; many corrupt ones resigned on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Officials under his command feared his stern authority, and many corrupt among them resigned of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 有勢家硃丹其門，聞瑞至，黝之。

translations.literal: A powerful family had painted their gate vermillion; when they heard Rui was coming, they blackened it.
translations.idiomatic: One influential household had painted its gate vermillion; on hearing that Rui was on his way, they hurriedly daubed it black.

sentences.zh: 中人監織造者，為減輿從。

translations.literal: Eunuchs supervising the imperial textile workshops reduced their retinues of carriages and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs overseeing the imperial weaving offices cut back their carriages and attendants.

sentences.zh: 瑞銳意興革，請浚吳淞、白茆，通流入海，民賴其利。

translations.literal: Rui was keen to reform; he requested dredging the Wusong and Baimao rivers to channel water into the sea, and the people relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Rui pressed hard for reform. He petitioned to dredge the Wusong and Baimao waterways so their currents could reach the sea, and the people prospered from the work.

sentences.zh: 素疾大戶兼併，力摧豪強，撫窮弱。

translations.literal: He had long hated large landholders' mergers; he strove to crush the powerful and comfort the weak.
translations.idiomatic: He had always detested the consolidation of estates by great families, and he worked relentlessly to break the mighty while sheltering the poor.

sentences.zh: 貧民田入于富室者，率奪還之。

translations.literal: Fields of poor peasants that had passed into wealthy households were for the most part seized back and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Land that poor farmers had lost to rich households was, as a rule, taken back and restored to them.

sentences.zh: 徐階罷相裏居，按問其家無少貸。

translations.literal: When Xu Jie was dismissed from the chancellorship and lived at home, Rui investigated his household and granted no indulgence whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: Even after Xu Jie had left office and retired to his home, Rui scrutinized his household and showed not the slightest leniency.

sentences.zh: 下令飆發淩厲，所司惴惴奉行，豪有力者至竄他郡以避。

translations.literal: His orders flew forth fierce and swift; the responsible offices obeyed in trembling fear, and powerful magnates fled to other prefectures to escape.
translations.idiomatic: His edicts issued with fierce urgency; the offices charged with carrying them out obeyed in dread, and the boldest local powers fled to neighboring prefectures to escape him.

sentences.zh: 而奸民多乘機告訐，故家大姓時有被誣負屈者。

translations.literal: Yet scheming commoners often seized the opportunity to denounce others; old great families were at times falsely accused and suffered injustice.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, unscrupulous men often seized the moment to lodge accusations, and established clans were sometimes falsely charged and wronged.

sentences.zh: 又裁節郵傳冗費。

translations.literal: He also cut redundant expenses in the courier and relay system.
translations.idiomatic: He also pared away wasteful spending in the postal and relay service.

sentences.zh: 士大夫出其境率不得供頓，由是怨頗興。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials passing through his jurisdiction generally could not receive lodging and provisions; resentment therefore grew considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Official travelers leaving his territory were usually denied the customary provisions and lodging, and ill will toward him mounted accordingly.

sentences.zh: 都給事中舒化論瑞，滯不達政體，宜以南京清秩處之，帝猶優詔獎瑞。

translations.literal: Chief Supervising Secretary Shu Hua discussed Rui, saying he was sluggish and did not grasp the substance of governance and ought to be placed in an honorary post at Nanjing; yet the Emperor still issued an edict praising Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Supervising Secretary Shu Hua argued that Rui was inflexible and failed to understand how government should work, and should be given a quiet honorary post in Nanjing—yet the Emperor still issued a gracious edict commending Rui.

sentences.zh: 已而給事中戴鳳翔劾瑞庇奸民，魚肉搢紳，沽名亂政，遂改督南京糧儲。

translations.literal: Before long, Supervising Secretary Dai Fengxiang impeached Rui for shielding scheming commoners, oppressing the gentry, seeking fame, and disrupting governance; he was then reassigned to supervise grain storage at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Supervising Secretary Dai Fengxiang accused Rui of protecting rascals, bullying the gentry, courting reputation, and sowing disorder in government, and Rui was transferred to oversee grain storage in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 瑞撫吳甫半歲。

translations.literal: Rui had governed Wu for only half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Hai Rui had governed the Wu region for barely six months.

sentences.zh: 小民聞當去，號泣載道，家繪像祀之。

translations.literal: When common folk heard he was to leave, they wept and wailed filling the roads; families painted his portrait to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: When the common people learned he was leaving, they wailed along every road, and households painted his likeness to honor him in worship.

sentences.zh: 將履新任，會高拱掌吏部，素銜瑞，並其職于南京戶部，瑞遂謝病歸。

translations.literal: About to take up his new post, it happened that Gao Gong was in charge of the Ministry of Personnel and had long harbored a grudge against Rui; he merged Rui's post into the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, and Rui then resigned citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was about to assume his new appointment, Gao Gong took charge of the Ministry of Personnel. Gao had long resented Rui and folded Rui's office into the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; Rui thereupon pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，張居正當國，亦不樂瑞，令巡按御史廉察之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, Zhang Juzheng held state power and was also displeased with Rui; he ordered the touring Investigating Censor to inspect him for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign, Zhang Juzheng directed the government and likewise had no fondness for Rui; he sent the touring censor to investigate his conduct.

sentences.zh: 御史至山中視，瑞設雞黍相對食，居舍蕭然，御史歎息去。

translations.literal: The censor went to the mountains to see him; Rui set out chicken and millet and they ate together; his dwelling was bare and sparse, and the censor sighed and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the censor came to see him in the hills, Rui offered a simple meal of chicken and millet and ate with him face to face. His home was plainly furnished and empty; the censor sighed and left.

sentences.zh: 居正憚瑞峭直，中外交薦，卒不召。

translations.literal: Juzheng feared Rui's uncompromising rectitude; though people inside and outside the court repeatedly recommended him, in the end he was not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng feared Rui's unyielding uprightness. Recommendations poured in from within and outside the court, yet in the end Rui was never recalled.

sentences.zh: 十二年冬，居正已卒，吏部擬用左通政。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twelfth year, Juzheng had already died; the Ministry of Personnel proposed appointing him Left Vice Commissioner of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twelfth year, after Zhang Juzheng's death, the Ministry of Personnel proposed appointing Rui Left Vice Commissioner of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 帝雅重瑞名，畀以前職。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly esteemed Rui's reputation and granted him his former position.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held Rui's name in high regard and restored him to his previous rank.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，召為南京右僉都御史，道改南京吏部右侍郎，瑞年已七十二矣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, he was summoned as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing; en route he was changed to Right Vice Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel—Rui was already seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the next year he was summoned as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing, then reassigned on the road to Right Vice Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel. Rui was already seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 疏言衰老垂死，願比古人屍諫之義，大略謂：「陛下勵精圖治，而治化不臻者，貪吏之刑輕也。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said he was aged and near death, wishing to follow the ancient principle of remonstrating with one's corpse; in general he stated: "Your Majesty strives with vigor to govern well, yet good order is not achieved—the reason is that corrupt officials receive light punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he declared that he was old and close to death and wished to follow the ancient example of remonstrating even with one's corpse. In essence he wrote: "Your Majesty labors tirelessly to bring order to the realm, yet good governance still falls short because corrupt officials are punished too lightly.

sentences.zh: 諸臣莫能言其故，反借待士有禮之說，交口而文其非。

translations.literal: None of the ministers can speak the reason; instead they borrow the doctrine that officials should be treated with courtesy, and with one voice embellish the wrong.
translations.idiomatic: No minister will say why this is so; instead they invoke the principle that scholars should be treated with courtesy and, speaking as one, dress up the fault as virtue.

sentences.zh: 夫待士有禮，而民則何辜哉？」

translations.literal: If officials are treated with courtesy, what crime have the common people committed?
translations.idiomatic: If courtesy is owed to officials, what wrong have the people done to deserve this?

sentences.zh: 因舉太祖法剝皮囊草及洪武三十年定律枉法八十貫論絞，謂今當用此懲貪。

translations.literal: He cited the founding Emperor's law of flaying the skin and stuffing it with straw, and the Hongwu thirtieth-year statute sentencing those who pervert the law for eighty strings of cash to death by strangulation, saying these should now be used to punish greed.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed to the founding Emperor's punishment of flaying the skin and stuffing it with straw, and to the thirtieth year of Hongwu statute that sentenced officials who perverted the law for eighty strings of cash to death by strangulation, arguing that these measures should be revived to chastise corruption.

sentences.zh: 其他規切時政，語極剴切。

translations.literal: On other matters too he admonished current policy; his words were extremely sharp and earnest.
translations.idiomatic: On other points as well he remonstrated against current affairs in language that was piercing and unsparing.

sentences.zh: 獨勸帝虐刑，時議以為非。

translations.literal: Only in urging harsh punishments upon the Emperor did contemporary opinion deem him wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Only his counsel that the Emperor impose cruel punishments was judged mistaken by opinion at the time.

sentences.zh: 御史梅鶤祚劾之。

translations.literal: Censor Mei Guizuo impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Mei Guizuo submitted an impeachment against him.

sentences.zh: 帝雖以瑞言為過，然察其忠誠，為奪鶤祚俸。

translations.literal: Though the Emperor considered Rui's words excessive, perceiving his loyalty he instead stripped Guizuo of his salary.
translations.idiomatic: Although the Emperor thought Rui had gone too far, he saw the sincerity behind the words and punished Guizuo by stripping his salary instead.

sentences.zh: 帝屢欲召用瑞，執政陰沮之，乃以為南京右都御史。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly wished to summon and employ Rui, but the chief ministers secretly obstructed him; Rui was then appointed Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wanted again and again to recall Rui to service, but those in power quietly blocked it, and Rui was given the post of Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 諸司素偷惰，瑞以身矯之。

translations.literal: The various offices were by nature lazy and negligent; Rui corrected them by his own example.
translations.idiomatic: The departments had long been slack and indolent; Rui set himself against the habit and reformed them by his own conduct.

sentences.zh: 有御史偶陳戲樂，欲遵太祖法予之杖。

translations.literal: When a censor casually mentioned theatrical entertainment, Rui wished to follow the founding Emperor's law and have him beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when a censor casually spoke of music and amusement, Rui wanted to apply the founding Emperor's law and have him flogged with the rod.

sentences.zh: 百司惴恐，多患苦之。

translations.literal: The hundred offices trembled in fear; many suffered and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Every office quaked with fear, and many found his rule hard to bear.

sentences.zh: 提學御史房寰恐見糾擿，欲先發，給事中鐘宇淳復慫恿，寰再上疏醜詆。

translations.literal: Education Intendant Censor Fang Huan feared being investigated and censured and wished to strike first; Supervising Secretary Zhong Yuchun again egged him on, and Huan submitted another memorial viciously slandering Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Education Intendant Censor Fang Huan, fearing he would be called out and punished, tried to get ahead of Rui; Supervising Secretary Zhong Yuchun urged him on again, and Fang submitted another memorial full of ugly abuse.

sentences.zh: 瑞亦屢疏乞休，慰留不允。

translations.literal: Rui also repeatedly submitted memorials requesting retirement, but reassurances to stay were not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Rui too sent memorial after memorial asking to retire, yet the court's pleas that he remain were never accepted.

sentences.zh: 十五年，卒官。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, he died at his post.

sentences.zh: 瑞無子。

translations.literal: Rui had no son.
translations.idiomatic: Rui left no son.

sentences.zh: 卒時，僉都御史王用汲入視，葛幃敝籝，有寒士所不堪者。

translations.literal: When he died, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yongji came to view his quarters: coarse hemp curtains and worn-out boxes—things even a poor scholar could scarcely endure.
translations.idiomatic: At his death, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yongji came to inspect his quarters and found coarse hemp curtains and battered chests—possessions a poor scholar could scarcely bear.

sentences.zh: 因泣下，醵金為斂。

translations.literal: He thereupon wept, and collected money for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: He wept and gathered a collection to pay for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 小民罷市。

translations.literal: The common people closed their markets.
translations.idiomatic: Shopkeepers shut their stalls in mourning.

sentences.zh: 喪出江上，白衣冠送者夾岸，酹而哭者百里不絕。

translations.literal: When the coffin went out onto the river, those in white dress lined both banks to see it off; those who poured libations and wept extended unbroken for a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: As the funeral procession moved along the river, mourners in white lined both banks; for a hundred li, none who poured libations and wept ceased their lamentation.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，諡忠介。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Loyal and Upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous epithet Zhongjie, 'Loyal and Upright.'

sentences.zh: 瑞生平為學，以剛為主，因自號剛峰，天下稱剛峰先生。

translations.literal: Throughout his life Rui pursued learning, taking rigidity as his principle; hence he styled himself Rigid Peak, and the world called him Master Rigid Peak.
translations.idiomatic: Rui built his life's learning on uncompromising integrity; he styled himself Gangfeng, 'Rigid Peak,' and the world knew him as Master Gangfeng.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「欲天下治安，必行井田。

translations.literal: He once said: 'If one wishes peace and order throughout the realm, the well-field system must be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He once declared: 'To bring peace and order to the realm, the well-field system must be restored.

sentences.zh: 不得已而限田，又不得已而均稅，尚可存古人遺意。」

translations.literal: If that cannot be done, then land limits; if that too cannot be done, then equalized taxation—even so, the ancients' intent may yet be preserved.'
translations.idiomatic: Failing that, impose land limits; failing even that, equalize taxation—by such steps the intent of the ancients may yet be preserved.

sentences.zh: 故自為縣以至巡撫，所至力行清丈，頒一條鞭法。

translations.literal: Therefore from his time as county magistrate through his service as grand coordinator, wherever he went he vigorously carried out land surveys and promulgated the single-whip tax system.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, from his days as a county magistrate through his tenure as grand coordinator, wherever he served he drove land surveys and implemented the single-whip method of taxation.

sentences.zh: 意主于利民，而行事不能無偏雲。

translations.literal: His intention lay chiefly in benefiting the people, yet in action he could not be wholly free from partiality, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: His aim was above all to benefit the people—yet even his admirers concede that his methods could not but show partiality.

sentences.zh: 何以尚

translations.literal: He Yishang
translations.idiomatic: He Yishang

sentences.zh: 始救瑞者何以尚，廣西興業人，起家鄉舉。

translations.literal: He who first rescued Rui was He Yishang, a man of Xingye in Guangxi, who began his career through the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: The man who first rescued Hai Rui was He Yishang, a native of Xingye in Guangxi who had entered office through the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 出獄，擢光祿丞。

translations.literal: Upon leaving prison, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Released from prison, he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 又以劾高拱坐謫。

translations.literal: He was again demoted on account of impeaching Gao Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished again after impeaching Gao Gong.

sentences.zh: 拱罷，起雷州推官，終南京鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: After Gong was dismissed, he was reinstated as judicial assistant of Leizhou and ended his career as Director of Ceremonials at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Gong fell, he was restored as judicial assistant at Leizhou and ended his days as director of ceremonies at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 丘橓，字茂實，諸城人。

translations.literal: Qiu Shun, styled Maoshi, was a man of Zhucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shun, styled Maoshi, was a native of Zhucheng.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十九年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He qualified as a metropolitan graduate in the twenty-ninth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 由行人擢刑科給事中。

translations.literal: From his post as courier he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: From the post of courier he was raised to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 三十四年七月，倭六七十人失道流劫，自太平直逼南京。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, seventh month, sixty or seventy pirates lost their way and roamed plundering, from Taiping straight to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year, seventh month, sixty or seventy pirates, having lost their way, swept through in a raid from Taiping straight to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書張時徹等閉城不敢出，閱二日引去。

translations.literal: Minister of War Zhang Shiche and others closed the city gates and dared not go out; after two days the pirates withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Zhang Shiche and his colleagues shut the city gates and dared not sally forth; after two days the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 給事御史劾時徹及守備諸臣罪，時徹亦上其事，詞多隱護。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries and censors impeached Shiche and the garrison officials; Shiche also submitted a report, his language largely concealing and protecting them.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censors impeached Shiche and the garrison commanders; Shiche submitted his own account as well, wording it largely to conceal and shield them.

sentences.zh: 舜劾其欺罔，時徹及侍郎陳洙皆罷。

translations.literal: Shun impeached him for deceit; Shiche and Vice Minister Chen Zhu were both dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Shun impeached him for deception; Shiche and Vice Minister Chen Zhu were both removed from office.

sentences.zh: 帝久不視朝，嚴嵩專國柄。

translations.literal: The emperor had long ceased holding court audiences; Yan Song monopolized state power.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long ceased to hold court; Yan Song held the reins of state alone.

sentences.zh: 橓言權臣不宜獨任，朝綱不宜久弛，嚴嵩深憾之。

translations.literal: Shun said that powerful ministers should not hold sole authority and that court discipline should not be slackened for long; Yan Song deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Shun argued that no single powerful minister should wield unchecked authority and that court discipline must not long lie in abeyance; Yan Song deeply resented him for it.

sentences.zh: 已，劾嵩党寧夏巡撫謝淮、應天府尹孟淮貪黷，謝淮坐免。

translations.literal: Later he impeached Yan Song's faction—Ningxia grand coordinator Xie Huai and Nanjing metropolitan prefect Meng Huai—for corruption and abuse; Xie Huai was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he impeached two men of Yan Song's faction—Ningxia grand coordinator Xie Huai and Nanjing metropolitan prefect Meng Huai—for corruption and abuse; Xie Huai was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 是年，嵩敗，舜劾由嵩進者順天巡撫徐紳等五人，帝為黜其三。

translations.literal: That year, when Yan Song fell, Shun impeached five men who had risen through Yan Song's patronage, including Shuntian grand coordinator Xu Shen; the emperor dismissed three of them.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, after Yan Song's fall, Shun impeached five officials who had risen through his patronage, including Shuntian grand coordinator Xu Shen; the emperor dismissed three of them.

sentences.zh: 遷兵科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief supervising secretary of the Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of War.

sentences.zh: 劾南京兵部尚書李遂、鎮守兩廣平江伯陳王謨、錦衣指揮魏大經鹹以賄進，大經下吏，王謨革任。

translations.literal: He impeached Nanjing Minister of War Li Sui, the commander-in-chief of the Two Guang, Pingjiang Earl Chen Wangmo, and Embroidered Uniform Guard commander Wei Dajing—all for having advanced through bribery; Dajing was sent to judicial custody and Wangmo was stripped of his post.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Nanjing Minister of War Li Sui, the commander-in-chief of the Two Guang, Pingjiang Earl Chen Wangmo, and Embroidered Uniform Guard commander Wei Dajing—all for having bought their way into office; Dajing was handed over to the courts and Wangmo was stripped of his command.

sentences.zh: 已，又劾罷浙江總兵官盧鏜。

translations.literal: Later he again impeached and caused the dismissal of Zhejiang regional commander Lu Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he impeached Zhejiang regional commander Lu Zuan and brought about his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 寇犯通州，總督楊選被逮。

translations.literal: When bandits invaded Tongzhou, Grand Coordinator Yang Xuan was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders struck Tongzhou, Grand Coordinator Yang Xuan was arrested.

sentences.zh: 及寇退，橓偕其僚陳善後事宜，指切邊弊。

translations.literal: After the bandits withdrew, Shun together with his colleagues memorialized on post-crisis arrangements, directly addressing border abuses.
translations.idiomatic: After the raiders withdrew, Shun and his colleagues jointly memorialized on the aftermath, cutting straight to the abuses along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 帝以橓不早劾選，杖六十，斥為民，余謫邊方雜職。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Shun had not impeached Xuan earlier, had him beaten sixty strokes and expelled as a commoner; the others were demoted to minor frontier posts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, holding that Shun should have impeached Xuan sooner, had him beaten sixty strokes and expelled to commoner status; the others were relegated to minor frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 橓歸，敝衣一篋，圖書一束而已。

translations.literal: When Shun returned home, he had only one basket of worn clothes and one bundle of books.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun went home, he possessed only a single basket of threadbare clothes and one bundle of books.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，起任禮科，不至。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was recalled to the Bureau of Rites but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Longqing reign he was recalled to the Bureau of Rites but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 尋擢南京太常少卿，進大理少卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing, then advanced to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing, then advanced to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 病免。

translations.literal: He resigned due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced his retirement.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，言官交薦。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, censorial officials repeatedly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong took the throne, censorial officials recommended him one after another.

sentences.zh: 張居正惡之，不召。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng disliked him and did not summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng, who despised him, refused to recall him.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十一年秋，起右通政。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eleventh year of Wanli he was recalled as Right Vice Commissioner of the Surveillance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eleventh year of Wanli he was recalled as right vice commissioner of the Surveillance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 未上，擢左副都御史，以一柴車就道。

translations.literal: Before he assumed that post, he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and set out with only a cart of firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up that post, he was promoted to left vice censor-in-chief and set out for the capital in a single cart of firewood.

sentences.zh: 既入朝，陳吏治積弊八事，言：

translations.literal: Having entered court, he presented eight longstanding abuses in official administration, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Once he had entered court, he laid out eight longstanding abuses in governance, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣去國十餘年，士風漸靡，吏治轉汙，遠近蕭條，日甚一日。

translations.literal: Your servant has been away from the capital for more than ten years; scholarly ethos has gradually decayed, official administration has turned corrupt, and desolation near and far grows worse day by day.
translations.idiomatic: I have been away from the capital for more than ten years; the spirit of the scholar-official class has slackened, governance has grown filthy, and desolation near and far worsens by the day.

sentences.zh: 此非世運適然，由風紀不振故也。

translations.literal: This is not simply the way of the times; it is because discipline and standards have not been enforced.
translations.idiomatic: This is no mere turn of fortune—it is because discipline and standards have not been upheld.

sentences.zh: 如京官考滿，河南道例書稱職。

translations.literal: For example, when capital officials complete their term evaluations, the Henan circuit routinely records them as 'competent.'
translations.idiomatic: Consider the capital officials' term evaluations: the Henan circuit routinely marks every man 'competent.'

sentences.zh: 外吏給由，撫按官概與保留。

translations.literal: When local officials receive their credentials, the provincial governors and surveillance commissioners invariably grant them retention in office.
translations.idiomatic: When local officials receive their credentials, the grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners invariably retain them in post.

sentences.zh: 以朝廷甄別之典，為人臣交市之資。

translations.literal: They turn the court's institution of evaluation and selection into capital for ministers' mutual deal-making.
translations.idiomatic: They have turned the court's system of evaluation and selection into currency for mutual favor-trading among officials.

sentences.zh: 敢徇私而不敢盡法，惡無所懲，賢亦安勸？

translations.literal: They dare show favoritism but dare not enforce the law fully—how can the wicked be punished, and how can the worthy be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: Men dare show partiality but dare not enforce the law to the full—how then are the wicked to be punished, or the worthy to be encouraged?

sentences.zh: 此考績之積弊，一也。

translations.literal: This is the first of the longstanding abuses in performance evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first of the longstanding abuses in performance evaluation.

sentences.zh: 御史巡方，未離國門，而密屬之姓名，已盈私牘。

translations.literal: When touring censors inspect the provinces, before they have left the capital gates, the names of those privately entrusted to them already fill private letters.
translations.idiomatic: When censors set out to inspect the provinces, even before they leave the capital the names of those who have privately enlisted their help already fill private letters.

sentences.zh: 甫臨所部，而請事之竿牘，又滿行台。

translations.literal: No sooner do they reach their jurisdiction than the bamboo slips of requests again fill the touring office.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly have they reached their jurisdiction when the bamboo slips of petitioners again fill the touring office.

sentences.zh: 以豸冠持斧之威，束手俯眉，聽人頤指。

translations.literal: Bearing the authority of the censor's cap and axe, they fold their hands and bow their brows, letting others command them as they please.
translations.idiomatic: Armed with the censor's cap and axe—the emblems of their authority—they fold their hands, bow their brows, and let others order them about at will.

sentences.zh: 此請托之積弊，二也。

translations.literal: This is the second longstanding abuse of patronage and entreaty.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second entrenched abuse: patronage and entreaty.

sentences.zh: 撫按定監司考語，必托之有司。

translations.literal: When provincial governors and surveillance commissioners fix the evaluation comments for circuit intendants, they invariably entrust this to local officials.
translations.idiomatic: When grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners draft evaluation comments for circuit intendants, they invariably delegate the task to local officials.

sentences.zh: 有司則不顧是非，侈加善考，監司德且畏之。

translations.literal: Those officials then disregard right and wrong and lavishly add favorable evaluations, and the circuit intendants both feel indebted and fear them.
translations.idiomatic: Those officials ignore right and wrong and heap on glowing evaluations, and the circuit intendants feel both indebted and intimidated.

sentences.zh: 彼此結納，上下之分蕩然。

translations.literal: Each side cultivates ties of mutual obligation, and the distinction between superior and subordinate is utterly dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Each side forges bonds of mutual obligation until the distinction between superior and subordinate is utterly lost.

sentences.zh: 其考守令也亦如是。

translations.literal: Their evaluation of prefects and magistrates follows the same pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Their evaluation of prefects and magistrates follows the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 此訪察之積弊，三也。

translations.literal: This is the third longstanding abuse of inspection and surveillance.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third entrenched abuse: inspection and surveillance.

sentences.zh: 貪墨成風，生民塗炭，而所劾罷者大都單寒軟弱之流。

translations.literal: Corruption has become the prevailing wind, and the common people suffer as if scorched by fire; yet those impeached and dismissed are mostly of humble and powerless sort.
translations.idiomatic: Corruption has become the prevailing wind and the common people suffer as if scorched by fire, yet those impeached and dismissed are mostly humble and powerless men.

sentences.zh: 苟百足之蟲，傅翼之虎，即贓穢狼籍，還登薦剡。

translations.literal: If one is a centipede or a tiger given wings, even when his corruption is notorious he still receives a recommendation dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: If a man is a centipede with a hundred legs or a tiger given wings, even when his corruption is notorious he still receives a recommendation dispatch.

sentences.zh: 嚴小吏而寬大吏，詳去任而略見任。

translations.literal: They are strict with petty clerks but lenient with grand officials, meticulous about those leaving office but lax about those still in office.
translations.idiomatic: They are strict with petty clerks but lenient with grand officials, meticulous about men leaving office but lax about men still in office.

sentences.zh: 此舉劾之積弊，四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth longstanding abuse of recommendation and impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth entrenched abuse: recommendation and impeachment.

sentences.zh: 懲貪之法在提問。

translations.literal: The law for punishing corruption lies in interrogation under torture.
translations.idiomatic: The law for punishing corruption lies in interrogation under torture.

sentences.zh: 乃豺狼見遺，狐狸是問，徒有其名。

translations.literal: Yet wolves and jackals are overlooked while foxes are questioned—there is only the name of the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Yet wolves and jackals are overlooked while foxes are questioned—the practice exists in name only.

sentences.zh: 或陰縱之使去，或累逮而不行，或批駁以相延，或朦朧以倖免。

translations.literal: Some are secretly allowed to flee; some are repeatedly summoned but never brought in; some cases are rejected by memorial to stall proceedings; some are left deliberately vague so the accused may escape by chance.
translations.idiomatic: Some are secretly allowed to flee; some are repeatedly summoned but never brought in; some cases are rejected by memorial to stall proceedings; some are left deliberately vague so the accused may slip free by chance.

sentences.zh: 即或終竟其事，亦必博長厚之名，而以盡法自嫌。

translations.literal: Even when a case is finally concluded, the judge must win a reputation for leniency and restraint and shrink from applying the full penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Even when a case is finally concluded, the judge must win a reputation for leniency and restraint and shrink from applying the full penalty.

sentences.zh: 苞苴或累萬金，而贓止坐之銖黍。

translations.literal: Bribes may amount to tens of thousands in gold, yet only grains and millet are charged as the sum of corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Bribes may amount to tens of thousands in gold, yet only grains and millet are charged as the sum of corruption.

sentences.zh: 草菅或數十命，而罰不傷其毫釐。

translations.literal: Dozens of lives may be treated like grass, yet the punishment does not touch a hair's breadth of the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of lives may be treated like grass, yet the punishment does not touch a hair's breadth of the guilty.

sentences.zh: 此提問之積弊，五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth longstanding abuse of interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth entrenched abuse: interrogation.

sentences.zh: 薦舉糾劾，所以勸儆有司也。

translations.literal: Recommendation and impeachment exist to warn and admonish local officials.
translations.idiomatic: Recommendation and impeachment exist to warn and admonish local officials.

sentences.zh: 今薦則先進士而舉監，非有憑藉者不與焉。

translations.literal: Today in recommendations, metropolitan degree-holders are promoted first and purchased-office holders only afterward; those without backing are excluded.
translations.idiomatic: Today in recommendations, metropolitan degree-holders are promoted first and purchased-office holders only afterward; those without backing are excluded.

sentences.zh: 劾則先舉監而進士，縱有訾議者罕及焉。

translations.literal: In impeachments, purchased-office holders are struck first and metropolitan degree-holders afterward; even when there is criticism, they rarely reach the latter.
translations.idiomatic: In impeachments, purchased-office holders are struck first and metropolitan degree-holders afterward; even when there is criticism, it rarely reaches the latter.

sentences.zh: 晉接差委，專計出身之途。

translations.literal: In daily reception and assignment of duties, everything turns on the path by which one entered officialdom.
translations.idiomatic: In daily reception and assignment of duties, everything turns on the path by which one entered officialdom.

sentences.zh: 於是同一官也，不敢接席而坐，比肩而行。

translations.literal: Thereupon officials of the same rank dare not sit on the same mat or walk shoulder to shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon officials of the same rank dare not sit on the same mat or walk shoulder to shoulder.

sentences.zh: 諸人自分低昂，吏民觀瞻頓異。

translations.literal: The men rank themselves high and low, and the view held by clerks and commoners is suddenly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: The men rank themselves high and low, and the view held by clerks and commoners is suddenly transformed.

sentences.zh: 助成驕縱之風，大喪賢豪之氣。

translations.literal: This helps foster a spirit of arrogance and indulgence and greatly erodes the confidence of worthy and heroic men.
translations.idiomatic: This helps foster a spirit of arrogance and indulgence and greatly erodes the confidence of worthy and heroic men.

sentences.zh: 此資格之積弊，六也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth longstanding abuse of qualification and seniority.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth entrenched abuse: qualification and seniority.

sentences.zh: 州縣佐貳雖卑，亦臨民官也，必待以禮，然後可責以法。

translations.literal: The assistant and second-rank posts in prefectures and districts, though low, are still officials who face the people; they must be treated with courtesy before they can be held accountable under the law.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant and second-rank posts in prefectures and districts, though low, are still officials who face the people; they must be treated with courtesy before they can be held accountable under the law.

sentences.zh: 今也役使譴訶，無殊輿隸。

translations.literal: Today they are ordered about and rebuked no differently than carriage footmen.
translations.idiomatic: Today they are ordered about and rebuked no differently than carriage footmen.

sentences.zh: 獨任其汙黷害民，不屑禁治。

translations.literal: Yet their corruption and harm to the people are left entirely to them alone, with no inclination to restrain or punish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their corruption and harm to the people are left entirely to them alone, with no inclination to restrain or punish.

sentences.zh: 禮與法兩失之矣。

translations.literal: Both courtesy and law are lost.
translations.idiomatic: Both courtesy and law are lost.

sentences.zh: 學校之職，賢才所關，今不問職業，而一聽其所為。

translations.literal: The duties of schools concern men of talent; today no one asks after their professional conduct but leaves them entirely to their own devices.
translations.idiomatic: The duties of schools concern men of talent; today no one asks after their professional conduct but leaves them entirely to their own devices.

sentences.zh: 及至考課，則曰「此寒官也」，概與上考。

translations.literal: When evaluations come, they say, "These are humble posts," and give them uniformly top marks.
translations.idiomatic: When evaluations come, they say, "These are humble posts," and give them uniformly top marks.

sentences.zh: 若輩知上官不我重也，則因而自棄；

translations.literal: When such men know their superiors do not value them, they abandon themselves accordingly;
translations.idiomatic: When such men know their superiors do not value them, they abandon themselves accordingly;

sentences.zh: 知上官必我憐也，又從而日偷。

translations.literal: when they know their superiors will surely pity them, they likewise grow more lax day by day.
translations.idiomatic: when they know their superiors will surely pity them, they likewise grow more lax day by day.

sentences.zh: 此處佐貳教職之積弊，七也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh longstanding abuse in handling assistant officials and teaching posts.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh entrenched abuse: the treatment of assistant officials and teaching posts.

sentences.zh: 科場取士，故有門生、座主之稱。

translations.literal: In the examination hall men of talent are selected, hence the terms pupil and examiner-patron.
translations.idiomatic: In the examination hall men of talent are selected, hence the terms pupil and examiner-patron.

sentences.zh: 若巡按，舉劾其職也。

translations.literal: For a touring censor, however, recommendation and impeachment are his proper duties.
translations.idiomatic: For a touring censor, however, recommendation and impeachment are his proper duties.

sentences.zh: 乃劾者不任其怨，舉者獨冒為恩。

translations.literal: Yet the impeacher does not bear the resentment, while the recommender alone claims the favor as his own.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the impeacher does not bear the resentment, while the recommender alone claims the favor as his own.

sentences.zh: 尊之為舉主，而以門生自居，筐篚問遺，終身不廢。

translations.literal: They honor him as recommender-patron and take the status of pupils upon themselves; gifts in baskets and cases continue for a lifetime without cease.
