translations.literal: Zhengyu took up the brush and judged: "If Huang Guangsheng deserves a posthumous title, then Hai Rui should be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyu took up the brush and judged: "If Huang Guangsheng deserves a posthumous title, then Hai Rui should be killed.

sentences.zh: 許論當諡，是沈煉當殺也。

translations.literal: If Xu Lun deserves a posthumous title, then Shen Lian should be killed.
translations.idiomatic: If Xu Lun deserves a posthumous title, then Shen Lian should be killed.

sentences.zh: 呂本當諡，是鄢懋卿、趙文華皆名臣，不當削奪也。」

translations.literal: If Lü Ben deserves a posthumous title, then Yan Maoqing and Zhao Wenhua are all famous ministers and should not be stripped."
translations.idiomatic: If Lü Ben deserves a posthumous title, then Yan Maoqing and Zhao Wenhua are all famous ministers and should not be stripped."

sentences.zh: 議上，舉朝韙之，而卒不行。

translations.literal: When the deliberation was submitted, the whole court approved it, yet in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When the deliberation was submitted, the whole court approved it, yet in the end it was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 初，一貫屬正域毋言通政司匿疏事。

translations.literal: Earlier Yiguan had instructed Zhengyu not to speak of the Transmission Office concealing memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yiguan had instructed Zhengyu not to speak of the Transmission Office concealing memorials.

sentences.zh: 及華勣疏上，正域主行勘。

translations.literal: When Hua Xun's memorial was submitted, Zhengyu advocated conducting an investigation.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Xun's memorial was submitted, Zhengyu advocated conducting an investigation.

sentences.zh: 一貫言親王不當勘，但當體訪。

translations.literal: Yiguan said an imperial prince should not be investigated but only discreetly inquired into.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan said an imperial prince should not be investigated but only discreetly inquired into.

sentences.zh: 正域曰：「事關宗室，台諫當亦言之。」

translations.literal: Zhengyu said: "The matter concerns the imperial clan; censorial and remonstrance officials should also speak."
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyu said: "The matter concerns the imperial clan; censorial and remonstrance officials should also speak."

sentences.zh: 一貫微笑曰：「台諫斷不言也。」

translations.literal: Yiguan smiled slightly and said: "Censorial and remonstrance officials will certainly not speak."
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan smiled slightly and said: "Censorial and remonstrance officials will certainly not speak."

sentences.zh: 及帝從勘議，楚王懼，奉百金為正域壽，且屬毋竟楚事，當酬萬金，正域嚴拒之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor followed the investigation proposal, the Prince of Chu was afraid and presented a hundred in gold as birthday gift for Zhengyu, and also entrusted him not to pursue the Chu affair, promising ten thousand in gold in return; Zhengyu sternly refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor followed the investigation proposal, the Prince of Chu was afraid and presented a hundred in gold as birthday gift for Zhengyu, and also entrusted him not to pursue the Chu affair, promising ten thousand in gold in return; Zhengyu sternly refused.

sentences.zh: 已而湖廣巡撫趙可懷、巡按應朝卿勘上，言詳審無左驗，而王氏持之堅，諸郡主縣主則雲「罔知真偽」，乞特遣官再問。

translations.literal: Before long Huguang Grand Coordinator Zhao Kehuai and Surveillance Commissioner Ying Chaoqing submitted their investigation, saying the examination was detailed but there was no corroborating evidence, while the Wang clan held firm; the various commandery princesses and district princesses said they "did not know true from false," and begged that officials be specially dispatched to inquire again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Huguang Grand Coordinator Zhao Kehuai and Surveillance Commissioner Ying Chaoqing submitted their investigation, saying the examination was detailed but there was no corroborating evidence, while the Wang clan held firm; the various commandery princesses and district princesses said they "did not know true from false," and begged that officials be specially dispatched to inquire again.

sentences.zh: 詔公卿雜議于西闕門，日晏乃罷。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the grand secretaries and ministers to deliberate jointly at the Western Gate; the sun set before they adjourned.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the grand secretaries and ministers to deliberate jointly at the Western Gate; the sun set before they adjourned.

sentences.zh: 議者三十七人，各具一單，言人人殊。

translations.literal: Thirty-seven deliberators each submitted a separate sheet, and everyone's words differed.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-seven men deliberated, each submitting his own sheet—and no two opinions matched.

sentences.zh: 李廷機以左侍郎代正域署部事，正域欲盡錄諸人議，廷機以辭太繁，先撮其要以上。

translations.literal: Li Tingji, as left vice minister, replaced Zhengyu in administering the ministry's affairs; Zhengyu wished to record all the deliberators' opinions in full, but Tingji, finding the language too verbose, first extracted the essentials and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingji, now left vice minister, took over the ministry from Zhengyu. Zhengyu wanted every opinion copied in full; Tingji thought the record too long and submitted only a summary.

sentences.zh: 一貫遂嗾給事中楊應文、御史康丕揚劾禮部壅閼群議，不以實聞。

translations.literal: Yiguan then incited Supervising Secretary Yang Yingwen and Censor Kang Piyang to impeach the Ministry of Rites for obstructing and hoarding the collective deliberation and not reporting the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan then incited Yang Yingwen and Kang Piyang to accuse the Ministry of Rites of suppressing the joint deliberation and withholding the truth.

sentences.zh: 正域疏辨，且發子木匿疏、一貫阻勘及楚王饋遺狀。

translations.literal: Zhengyu memorialized in defense and also exposed Zimu's concealment of memorials, Yiguan's obstruction of the investigation, and the Prince of Chu's gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyu answered with a defense memorial that also exposed how Zimu had hidden memorials, how Yiguan had blocked the investigation, and the bribes offered by the Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 一貫益恚，謂正域遣家人導華勣上疏，議令楚王避位聽勘，私庇華勣。

translations.literal: Yiguan grew even more enraged and said Zhengyu had sent family members to guide Hua Xun in submitting his memorial, deliberated that the Prince of Chu should vacate his seat and await investigation, and privately shielded Hua Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan's rage deepened. He claimed Zhengyu had coached Hua Xun to submit his memorial, had pushed for the prince to step aside pending investigation, and was secretly protecting Hua Xun.

sentences.zh: 當是時，正域右宗人，大學士沈鯉右正域，尚書趙世卿、謝傑、祭酒黃汝良則右楚王。

translations.literal: At that time Zhengyu sided with the clansmen, Grand Secretary Shen Li sided with Zhengyu, and Ministers Zhao Shiqing, Xie Jie, and Chancellor Huang Ruliang sided with the Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyu backed the clansmen; Shen Li backed Zhengyu; Zhao Shiqing, Xie Jie, and Huang Ruliang backed the Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 給事中錢夢皋遂希一貫指論正域，詞連次輔鯉。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Qian Menggao then followed Yiguan's lead to attack Zhengyu, his words implicating the second grand secretary Li.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Menggao then took Yiguan's cue and attacked Zhengyu, dragging the second grand secretary Li into the accusation.

sentences.zh: 應文又言正域父懋嘗笞辱于楚恭王，故正域因事陷之。

translations.literal: Yingwen again said Zhengyu's father Mao had once been flogged and humiliated by the Prince of Chu's father, therefore Zhengyu used the affair to trap him.
translations.idiomatic: Yingwen added that Zhengyu's father Mao had once been beaten and shamed by the Prince of Chu's father—hence Zhengyu's vendetta.

sentences.zh: 正域疏辨，留中不報。

translations.literal: Zhengyu memorialized in defense; the memorial was kept within and no response given.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyu submitted another defense; the memorial was shelved without reply.

sentences.zh: 一貫、鯉以楚事皆求去，廷機復請再問。

translations.literal: Yiguan and Li both sought to leave over the Chu affair; Tingji again requested further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Both Yiguan and Li tried to resign over the Chu case; Tingji again asked for a fresh investigation.

sentences.zh: 帝以王嗣位二十餘年，何至今始發，且夫訐妻證，不足憑，遂罷楚事勿按。

translations.literal: The Emperor said the prince had held succession for more than twenty years—why raise this only now?—and that denunciation by a wife's testimony was insufficient to rely on; he therefore dropped the Chu affair without investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said the prince had reigned more than twenty years—why bring this up now?—and that a wife's accusation was no proof. The Chu case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 正域四疏乞休去。

translations.literal: Zhengyu submitted four memorials begging to retire and leave.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyu sent four memorials begging to be dismissed and go home.

sentences.zh: 楚王既得安，遂奏劾正域，大略如應文言；

translations.literal: Once the Prince of Chu was secure, he memorialized to impeach Zhengyu, in general terms like Yingwen's words;
translations.idiomatic: Once safe, the Prince of Chu memorialized against Zhengyu, echoing Yingwen's charges;

sentences.zh: 且訐其不法數事，請褫正域官。

translations.literal: he also denounced several unlawful acts and requested that Zhengyu be stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: he listed several crimes and asked that Zhengyu be stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 詔下部院集議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ministries and courts to deliberate jointly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the ministries and courts to meet and decide.

sentences.zh: 廷機微刺正域，而謂其已去，可無苛求。

translations.literal: Tingji subtly criticized Zhengyu but said that since he had already left, there need be no harsh demands.
translations.idiomatic: Tingji offered a veiled rebuke of Zhengyu but argued that, since he was already gone, no further punishment was needed.

sentences.zh: 給事中張問達則謂籓王欲進退大臣，不可訓，乃不罪正域，而令巡按御史勘王所訐以聞。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Wenda said a feudal prince should not advance or dismiss grand ministers and could not be admonished; therefore Zhengyu was not punished, but the touring surveillance censor was ordered to investigate what the prince had denounced and report.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenda said a prince had no business trying to remove a chief minister and could not be lectured like a subject. Zhengyu went unpunished, but a touring censor was told to verify the prince's charges.

sentences.zh: 俄而妖書事起。

translations.literal: Before long the affair of the demonic book arose.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward came the demonic-book scandal.

sentences.zh: 一貫以鯉與己地相逼，而正域新罷，因是陷之，則兩人必得重禍，乃為帝言臣下有欲相傾者為之。

translations.literal: Yiguan, because Li's territory pressed against his own and Zhengyu had just been dismissed, therefore framed them—then the two would surely suffer heavy calamity—and told the Emperor that among his ministers there were those who wished to destroy one another who had done this.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan, whose power bordered Li's and who had just seen Zhengyu fall, saw a chance to destroy them both. He hinted to the Emperor that rival ministers were plotting against one another.

sentences.zh: 蓋微引其端，以動帝意。

translations.literal: He subtly led with this point to move the Emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: He planted the suggestion carefully to sway the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 亡何，錦衣衛都督王之禎等四人以妖書有名，指其同官周嘉慶為之。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Zhizhen and three other commanders of the Embroidered Uniform Guard named in the demonic book pointed to their colleague Zhou Jiaqing as the author.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Zhizhen and three fellow commanders of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, also named in the book, accused their colleague Zhou Jiaqing of writing it.

sentences.zh: 東廠又捕獲妖人皦生光。

translations.literal: The Eastern Depot also captured the demonic man Jiao Shenguang.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Depot also arrested a man called Jiao Shenguang, linked to the book.

sentences.zh: 巡城御史康丕揚為生光訟冤，言妖書、楚事同一根柢，請少緩其獄，賊兄弟可授首闕下。

translations.literal: Kang Piyang, censor patrolling the city, pleaded Shenguang's innocence, saying the demonic book and the Chu affair shared the same root and begging that the case be slightly delayed so the bandit brothers could deliver their heads below the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Piyang, on city patrol, pleaded for Shenguang and said the book and the Chu case sprang from the same plot. Delay the trial, he urged, and the real culprits would soon lose their heads at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 意指正域及其兄國子監丞正位。

translations.literal: His meaning pointed at Zhengyu and his elder brother Zhengwei, superintendent of the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: He meant Zhengyu and his elder brother Zhengwei, superintendent of the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，以為庇反賊，除其名。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged, thinking he was shielding rebels, and struck his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, believing he was protecting traitors, struck Kang from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 一貫力救始免。

translations.literal: Yiguan strove to save him and he was finally spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan intervened and Kang was spared dismissal.

sentences.zh: 丕揚乃先後捕僧人達觀、醫者沈令譽等，而同知胡化則告妖書出教官阮明卿手。

translations.literal: Piyang then successively arrested the monk Daguang, the physician Shen Lingyu, and others, while Vice Prefect Hu Hua reported that the demonic book came from the hand of Instructor Ruan Mingqing.
translations.idiomatic: Piyang went on to arrest the monk Daguang, the physician Shen Lingyu, and others. Vice Prefect Hu Hua claimed the book had been written by Instructor Ruan Mingqing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，廠衛又捕可疑者一人曰毛尚文。

translations.literal: Before long the factory and guard also arrested a suspicious man named Mao Shangwen.
translations.idiomatic: The factory and guard soon seized another suspect, Mao Shangwen.

sentences.zh: 數日間鋃鐺旁午，都城人人自危。

translations.literal: Within a few days shackles clanked incessantly and everyone in the capital feared for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the clank of shackles filled the capital and no one felt safe.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶等皆下詔獄。

translations.literal: Jiaqing and the others were all sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing and the rest were thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶旋以治無驗，令革任回籍。

translations.literal: Jiaqing was soon found innocent upon investigation and ordered dismissed from office and returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation cleared Jiaqing; he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 令譽故嘗往來正域家，達觀亦時時游貴人門，嘗為正域所搒逐，尚文則正域僕也。

translations.literal: Lingyu had formerly come and gone at Zhengyu's house; Daguang also at times visited the gates of the powerful and had once been flogged and driven off by Zhengyu; Shangwen was Zhengyu's servant.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyu had frequented Zhengyu's house; Daguang had visited great men's gates and once been beaten and expelled by Zhengyu; Shangwen was Zhengyu's servant.

sentences.zh: 一貫、丕揚等欲自數人口引正域，而化所訐阮明卿，則錢夢皋婿。

translations.literal: Yiguan, Piyang, and the others wished to lead from many mouths to Zhengyu, while the Ruan Mingqing denounced by Hua was Qian Menggao's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan and Piyang hoped to tie many tongues to Zhengyu. The Ruan Mingqing named by Hu Hua was Qian Menggao's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 夢皋大恚，上疏顯攻正域，言：「妖書刊播，不先不後，適在楚王疏入之時。

translations.literal: Menggao was greatly enraged and submitted a memorial openly attacking Zhengyu, saying: "The demonic book was printed and circulated neither before nor after—it happened precisely when the Prince of Chu's memorial was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Menggao, furious, openly attacked Zhengyu: "The book appeared neither earlier nor later—it surfaced the very day the Prince of Chu's memorial went in.

sentences.zh: 蓋正域乃沈鯉門徒，而沈令譽者，正域食客，胡化又其同鄉同年，群奸結為死黨。

translations.literal: Zhengyu is a disciple of Shen Li, and Shen Lingyu is Zhengyu's retainer; Hu Hua is also their fellow townsman and examination-year mate—a gang of villains bound in a death pact.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyu is Shen Li's protégé; Lingyu is his client; Hu Hua is their townsman and classmate—a cabal sworn to ruin their enemies.

sentences.zh: 乞窮治根本，定正域亂楚首惡之罪，勒鯉閑住。」

translations.literal: I beg that the root be thoroughly pursued, that Zhengyu be fixed with the capital crime of disturbing Chu, and that Li be ordered to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: I beg a full inquiry, the death penalty for Zhengyu as the ringleader who stirred up Chu, and that Li be forced into retirement.

sentences.zh: 帝令正域還籍聽勘，急嚴訊諸所捕者。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Zhengyu to return to his native place and await investigation and urgently to interrogate severely all who had been arrested.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Zhengyu home to await trial and ordered harsh interrogation of every prisoner.

sentences.zh: 達觀拷死，令譽亦幾死，皆不承。

translations.literal: Daguang was tortured to death; Lingyu also nearly died—neither confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Daguang died under torture; Lingyu nearly did too. Neither would confess.

sentences.zh: 法司迫化引正域及歸德。

translations.literal: The judicial offices pressed Hua to implicate Zhengyu and Guidé.
translations.idiomatic: The courts pressed Hu Hua to name Zhengyu and Guidé.

sentences.zh: 歸德，鯉所居縣也。

translations.literal: Guidé was the county where Li lived.
translations.idiomatic: Guidé was Li's home county.

sentences.zh: 化大呼曰：「明卿，我仇也，故訐之。

translations.literal: Hua cried out loudly: "Mingqing is my enemy, therefore I denounced him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu shouted: "Mingqing is my enemy—that is why I accused him.

sentences.zh: 正域舉進士二十年不通問，何由同作妖書？

translations.literal: Zhengyu passed the metropolitan examination twenty years ago and we have had no contact—how could we together make a demonic book?
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyu passed his exams twenty years ago and we have never spoken—how could we plot together?

sentences.zh: 我亦不知誰為歸德者。」

translations.literal: I also do not know who the Guidé person is."
translations.idiomatic: I do not even know who this Guidé man is."

sentences.zh: 帝知化枉，釋之。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew Hua was wronged and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the injustice, the Emperor set Hu free.

sentences.zh: 都督陳汝忠掠訊尚文，遂發卒圍正域舟於楊村，盡捕媼婢及傭書者男女十五人，與生光雜治，終無所得。

translations.literal: Commander Chen Ruzhong interrogated Shangwen under torture and then dispatched soldiers to surround Zhengyu's boat at Yangcun, seizing entirely fifteen women and men among wet nurses, maidservants, and copyists, and tried them together with Shenguang—yet in the end nothing was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ruzhong tortured Shangwen, then sent troops to surround Zhengyu's boat at Yangcun. They seized fifteen servants and scribes, male and female, and tried them with Shenguang—but got nothing.

sentences.zh: 汝忠以錦衣告身誘尚文曰：「能告賊，即得之。」

translations.literal: Ruzhong used an Embroidered Uniform Guard commission to entice Shangwen, saying: "If you can denounce the villain, you will obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhong offered Shangwen an Guard commission: "Denounce the culprit and it is yours.

sentences.zh: 令引令譽，且以乳媼龔氏十歲女為徵。

translations.literal: He ordered him to implicate Lingyu and also used the ten-year-old daughter of wet nurse Gong as evidence.
translations.idiomatic: He told Shangwen to name Lingyu and produced the wet nurse Gong's ten-year-old daughter as a witness.

sentences.zh: 比會訊，東廠太監陳矩詰女曰：「汝見妖書版有幾？」

translations.literal: At the joint interrogation, Eastern Depot eunuch Chen Ju questioned the girl: "How many printing blocks for the demonic book did you see?
translations.idiomatic: At the joint hearing, the eunuch Chen Ju asked the girl: "How many blocks for the book did you see?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「盈屋。」

translations.literal: She said: "They filled the room."
translations.idiomatic: Enough to fill the room," she said.

sentences.zh: 矩笑曰：「妖書僅二三紙，版顧盈屋邪？」

translations.literal: Ju laughed and said: "The demonic book was only two or three sheets—could the blocks fill a room?"
translations.idiomatic: Ju laughed. "The book was two or three pages—could blocks fill a room?"

sentences.zh: 詰尚文曰：「令譽語汝刊書何日？」

translations.literal: He questioned Shangwen: "On what day did Lingyu tell you to print the book?"
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Shangwen: "What day did Lingyu tell you to print it?"

sentences.zh: 尚文曰：「十一月十六日。」

translations.literal: Shangwen said: "The sixteenth day of the eleventh month."
translations.idiomatic: The sixteenth of the eleventh month," Shangwen said.

sentences.zh: 戎政尚書王世揚曰；

translations.literal: Minister of War Wang Shiyang said;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Wang Shiyang objected;

sentences.zh: 「妖書以初十日獲，而十六日又刊，將有兩妖書邪？」

translations.literal: "The demonic book was seized on the tenth day, yet on the sixteenth it was printed again—will there be two demonic books?
translations.idiomatic: "You seized the book on the tenth, yet it was printed again on the sixteenth—are there two books?

sentences.zh: 拷生光妻妾及十歲兒，以針刺指爪，必欲引正域，皆不應。

translations.literal: They tortured Shenguang's wife, concubines, and ten-year-old child, piercing fingers and nails with needles, determined to lead the case to Zhengyu—all refused to answer.
translations.idiomatic: They tortured Shenguang's wife, concubines, and ten-year-old child, driving needles into fingers and nails to force a link to Zhengyu. None would speak.

sentences.zh: 生光仰視夢皋、丕揚，大罵曰：「死則死耳，奈何教我迎相公指，妄引郭侍郎乎？」

translations.literal: Shenguang looked up at Menggao and Piyang and cursed loudly: "Die then die—why teach me to follow the chief minister's finger and falsely implicate Vice Minister Guo?"
translations.idiomatic: Shenguang glared at Menggao and Piyang and cursed: "Kill me if you will—why make me lie and frame Vice Minister Guo at the chief minister's bidding?"

sentences.zh: 都御史溫純等力持之，事漸解，然猶不能具獄。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun and others strove to hold the line; the affair gradually dissolved, yet still they could not complete the case.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun and others held firm; the case began to collapse, though no full verdict could be reached.

sentences.zh: 光宗在東宮，數語近侍曰：「何為欲殺我好講官？」

translations.literal: The heir apparent, in the Eastern Palace, several times told his close attendants: "Why do they wish to kill my good lecturer?
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Palace the heir apparent told his attendants more than once: "Why do they want to kill my teacher?

sentences.zh: 諸人聞之皆懼。

translations.literal: When the others heard this they were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard it were terrified.

sentences.zh: 詹事唐文獻偕其僚楊道賓等詣一貫爭之，李廷機亦力為之地，獄益解。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Tang Wenxian together with his colleagues Yang Daobin and others went to argue with Yiguan; Li Tingji also forcefully intervened on his behalf, and the case dissolved further.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Tang Wenxian, Yang Daobin, and others confronted Yiguan; Li Tingji also fought for Zhengyu, and the prosecution unraveled further.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書蕭大亨具爰書，猶欲坐正域。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Xiao Daheng prepared the final judgment and still wished to convict Zhengyu.
translations.idiomatic: Justice Minister Xiao Daheng drafted the verdict and still wanted Zhengyu convicted.

sentences.zh: 郎中王述古抵稿于地，大亨乃止。

translations.literal: Director Wang Shugu dashed the draft to the ground; Daheng then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wang Shugu threw the draft on the floor; Daheng backed down.

sentences.zh: 遂坐生光極刑，釋諸波及者，而正域獲免。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shenguang was given the extreme penalty, those swept up in the affair were released, and Zhengyu escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Shenguang alone was executed; the rest were freed; Zhengyu was spared.

sentences.zh: 方獄急時，邏卒圍鯉舍及正域舟，鈴柝達旦。

translations.literal: When the case was urgent, courier soldiers surrounded Li's residence and Zhengyu's boat, and watch-clappers sounded until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of the crisis, couriers ringed Li's house and Zhengyu's boat, watch-clappers sounding all night.

sentences.zh: 又聲言正域且逮，迫使自裁。

translations.literal: There were also rumors that Zhengyu would soon be arrested, forcing him to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that arrest was imminent, pressuring Zhengyu to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 正域曰：「大臣有罪，當伏屍都市，安能自屏野外？」

translations.literal: Zhengyu said: "When a grand minister is guilty, he should lie dead in the marketplace—how can he hide himself in the wilds?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyu replied: "If a minister is guilty, let him die in the open market—he does not slink off to die in the wilderness."

sentences.zh: 既而幸無事，乃歸。

translations.literal: Afterward, fortunately suffering no incident, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the end nothing happened, and he went home.

sentences.zh: 歸三年，巡按御史史學遷勘上楚王所訐事，無狀。

translations.literal: Three years after his return, Touring Surveillance Censor Shi Xueqian submitted his investigation of what the Prince of Chu had denounced—there was no substance.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, touring censor Shi Xueqian reported on the Prince of Chu's charges: nothing held up.

sentences.zh: 給事顧士琦因請召還正域，不報。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Gu Shiqi therefore requested that Zhengyu be recalled; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shiqi asked that Zhengyu be recalled; the court did not answer.

sentences.zh: 正域博通載籍，勇於任事，有經濟大略，自守介然，故人望歸之。

translations.literal: Zhengyu was broadly learned in the classics and histories, bold in undertaking affairs, possessed of great economic vision, and upright in self-restraint—therefore men's esteem returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyu was deeply read, fearless in office, far-sighted in policy, and incorruptibly self-contained—men looked to him with respect.

sentences.zh: 扼于權相，遂不復起，家居十年卒。

translations.literal: Throttled by the powerful chief minister, he never rose again; he lived at home for ten years and died.
translations.idiomatic: Crushed by the chief minister's faction, he never served again. He lived at home ten years and died.

sentences.zh: 後四年，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Four years later he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Four years after his death he was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 光宗遺詔，加恩舊學，贈太子少保，諡文毅，官其子中書舍人。

translations.literal: The Taichang Emperor's deathbed edict added favor to his old teachers; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous epithet Wenyi, and his son was appointed Secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Taichang Emperor's deathbed grace honored his old tutors: Zhengyu was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent posthumously, given the epithet Wenyi, and his son received a post in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：海瑞秉剛勁之性，戇直自遂，蓋可希風漢汲黯、宋包拯。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Hai Rui possessed a nature of firm rigidity, blunt and straight in following his own course—he may be compared in spirit to Han's Ji An and Song's Bao Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Hai Rui was rigid and blunt, going his own way without compromise—in spirit he recalls Han's Ji An and Song's Bao Zheng.

sentences.zh: 苦節自厲，誠為人所難能。

translations.literal: He disciplined himself through bitter integrity—truly what others find hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: His austere self-discipline was something few could match.

sentences.zh: 丘橓、呂坤，雖非瑞匹，而指陳時政，炳炳鑿鑿，鯁亮有足稱者。

translations.literal: Qiu Shun and Lu Kun, though not Hai Rui's equal, in pointing out and setting forth the politics of their times were bright and penetrating, firm and bright—worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shun and Lu Kun did not equal Hai Rui, yet in diagnosing the ills of their age they spoke with clarity and courage and deserve remembrance.

sentences.zh: 郭正域持楚獄，與執政異趣，險難忽發，慬而後免，危矣哉！

translations.literal: Guo Zhengyu held to the Chu case against the chief minister's inclination; sudden peril erupted and only after utmost effort did he escape—how dangerous!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhengyu stood his ground on the Chu case against the chief minister; disaster struck suddenly and he barely survived—how close it was!

sentences.zh: 以妖書事與坤相首尾，故並著焉。

translations.literal: Because the demonic book affair and Kun's case began and ended together, they are therefore recorded together.
translations.idiomatic: Because the demonic-book scandal and Lu Kun's affair rose and fell together, both are told here.
